utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Registrar, could you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Thank you, and good afternoon, Your Honours. This is case number IT-03-67-T, the Prosecutor versus Vojislav Seselj.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Registrar. This is Wednesday, and I welcome all the representatives from the OTP and Mr. Seselj as well, of course, as our witness. Mr. Seselj, you have the floor for your cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. VS-1058, yesterday we stated together and we established why the volunteers of the Serbian Radical Party were sent to Eastern Slavonia. You confirmed that the main and the only reason was to defend the threat on Serbian villages; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1058 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: However, I expect from you to know, like the whole of Serbia knows, that I personally and the Serbian Radical Party that I belonged to before the war, during the war, and after the war that we advocated the ideology of a Greater Serbia; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1058 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: However, it would be ridiculous to go to Sodolovci, or to Ernestinovo, Laslovo, or Tenja, or Borovo Selo, and to create a Greater Serbia there; wouldn't that be ridiculous?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1058 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think I understood your question properly.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: In order to create a Greater Serbia, one would have to encompass the entire area inhabited by Serbs, the Orthodox Serbs, Muslim Serbs, and Catholic Serbs, and not only just a few villages in the eastern part of Slavonia where we sent volunteers before the JNA entered the war. Did you hear of any other volunteers being sent anywhere else but Eastern Slavonia before 1991?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1058 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Are you aware that we indeed are proponents of a Greater Serbia, my party, the Serbian Radical Party, and myself? Do you have any doubts about it that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1058 [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you say so, in principle I am not interested in politics. I am -- I don't engage in politics.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: However, nobody told you in Belgrade that you were being sent to fight for a Greater Serbia. You went and you had been told that you were being sent to defend the Serbian villages threatened by the newly established Ustasha government in Croatia?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1058 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. If anybody had told me that that was the idea, I would not have gone.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Well, nobody told you to do that, and we have established that. And now you saw in your statement in several places and you denied the fact that the Prosecutor who typed the statement on your behalf and you signed it, he insisted on a Greater Serbia and my alleged speeches to volunteers. Wouldn't it be ridiculous to say that if about ten of you were sitting in a room that I entered that room and gave a speech about a Greater Serbia; wouldn't that be ridiculous?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1058 [Resumed]
utterances.text: You are right there, but I repeat I did not hear you giving a speech. I never heard you say something like that to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: So you completely deny what is contained in your statement and concerns my speech about a Greater Serbia?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1058 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That part and the part where you are mentioned as my leader. Let me just explain one thing. I don't want the Trial Chamber or anybody else to think that I lie or that I'm here to change my statements, but yesterday we detected four mistakes -- actually, I detected just two. I was hardly waiting to be sent home, and I may have missed the other two mistakes. I didn't pay any -- much attention. If I had seen them, then I would have corrected the Prosecutor there and then, but I omitted to do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: It is my conviction that you presented the facts, that you were very precise when you provided your statement, and that you were a reliable person. There's not much for me to deny with regard to the facts that you presented. But your first interview lasted two days; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1058 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1058 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let's avoid any mistakes. It was not two days in a row.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: It says here on the 21st and 22nd April, 2004?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1058 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that there was one day break between the two days, but I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: I am more inclined to believe you than the OTP, but it says here 21 and 22 April.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1058 [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean 2004? In that case it's possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And on the -- at the end of day two you were given the statement in English?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1058 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And you read that statement?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1058 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I read it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And you speak enough English to be able to maintain a communication? That's what I concluded.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1058 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can communicate to a certain extent, but I can read much better. I work with computers and I need English for that. But what I'm saying is that I omitted that mistake.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: But did you read everything attentively, every page?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1058 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I was hardly waiting to be sent home.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: So you just glanced and skimmed through the statement and then you signed it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1058 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that I corrected one or two mistakes, I'm not sure. And then that was that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: But nobody actually read the Serbian translation back to you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1058 [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I remember, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1058 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was six years ago, so please do not --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could you please slow down, Mr. Witness and Mr. Seselj. You have to slow down. It's almost impossible for the interpreters to follow you. You're much too fast.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And please make a break between the question and the answer. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: So when the statement was over, it was given to you to read in English, which is not your mother tongue, and you signed it without reading the Serbian translation; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1058 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't be sure that -- it is possible that I also saw the Serbian translation. It was six years ago, so I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: So if it is possible that you saw the Serbian translation, I'm sure that nobody actually read the translation to you out loud?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1058 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't read it myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And here the OTP has deceived you and told you that you actually confirmed that the statement had been read back to you in the Serbian language, and you do not remember at all that the statement was read to you in the Serbian language in 2004?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1058 [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I've just told you, it was six years ago. I really can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Very well. And then you were again called on 2006 and you were invited to come for just one day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1058 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And when you spoke with Dan Saxon and Marie Costello, how long did your conversation last on that occasion?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1058 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't be sure. Maybe a couple of hours, two hours. Or perhaps three, I'm not sure. Or maybe even longer. I really can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Mr. Seselj's microphone is not on.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: I will repeat my question. Did -- on the second occasion when you met with the OTP, did you read the statement yourself or was the statement interpreted to you by the Prosecutors? Did they read the statement to you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1058 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that I read the statement, and we spoke about a few issues. I'm not sure. I can't remember, I'm telling you. I can't remember those interviews. I virtually forgot all about them until my memory was jogged here.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: So if you don't remember, I will no longer insist on those interviews. There's no need for that. The first time you came to Belgrade you could not be sent to Eastern Slavonia because the capacity for the training centre in Prigrevica was full. You spent a couple of days -- you slept in the party premises, and then you returned to Smederevo?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1058 [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the first occasion, I believe that I stayed two days.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And the next time you were invited to come, you came with your own weapons; it was a German make, Smajser, automatic weapon, as far as I could understand?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1058 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: It was a trophy from the Second World War?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1058 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: When you arrived at the headquarters of the party, did they tell you that you couldn't go to the bus with that automatic rifle but that somebody would bring that automatic rifle subsequently to you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1058 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Did they explain to you that you could not take the weapon on to the bus because the police might stop you and then that would be a problem because there would be a lot of questions about where you were going and why you were armed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1058 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Did you know that at the time we sent volunteers hiding that fact from the police of Serbia?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1058 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we were told that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: So that means that you travelled on the bus without any uniforms, without any weapons, and the fact was hidden from the police?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1058 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And then you arrived in Prigrevica. On the way, the bus took some scenic routes to avoid being noticed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1058 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The journey was long, but I didn't notice that fact because I was not familiar with the route.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: You arrived in Prigrevica in an abandoned farm, and that was the centre for the training of volunteers; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1058 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And you stayed for two weeks in training?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1058 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I believe so.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And the training was enough for you to jog your memory about what you had learned in the army because all of you had been in compulsory military training before the war?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1058 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And in Prigrevica you trained with very old weapons; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1058 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, those were old M-48 rifles.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: That's the old rifle that had been used by the JNA but was withdrawn from use?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1058 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Was there any other old weapons that were used there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1058 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't think so. I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: In one place in your statement you say that a general came to that centre and Milan Paroski, the two of them came to the centre for training?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1058 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Does it mean that in addition to members of the Serbian Radical Party in Prigrevica there were members of other parties as well?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1058 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Did you hear of Jovo Ostojic; does the name ring a bell?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1058 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Was he your boss in that training centre in Prigrevica?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1058 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was a local as far as I could tell, and he assisted. He took care of the supplies, the food.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: He was in charge for -- together with the instructors?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1058 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Do you know that Jovo Ostojic was at the time a member of the Serbian Democratic Party for Serbia?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1058 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Did you hear that maybe a year later he became a member of the Serbian Radical Party and became an MP?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1058 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard his name mentioned on TV several times. I saw him on a few occasions, but I did not put two and two together.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Did you hear that because of the war merits I proclaimed him the Serbian Chetnik Vojvoda?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1058 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard that. I didn't know if it was true.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: It was true, and I'm very proud of that because he deserves that merit. Did you see members of the Serbian Renewal Movement, Paroski, the Serbian National Renewal, and some other parties?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1058 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: There were members of the Serbian Renewal Movement for a while until Vuk Draskovic decided to establish his own paramilitary formation, Serbian card [as interpreted], and then he stopped sending volunteers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1058 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Do you remember that Draskovic appointed the worst criminals from Belgrade as commanders of that paramilitary army?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1058 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Do you know that we, representatives of different opposition parties, previously made an agreement with the associations of -- the Association of Serbs from Croatia to jointly send the volunteers and train them in that centre in Prigrevica?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1058 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. Believe me, I wasn't -- was not aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: You said that there were approximately 70 per cent members of the Serbian Radical Party and some 30 per cent of all the others, if I remember your statement correctly?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1058 [Resumed]
utterances.text: To be honest, I didn't count heads. It is possible that most of us were Radicals, but I can't be sure. I can't tell you exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And the general that came to visit you, you didn't know his name?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1058 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And if I tell you that that was the famous partisan general, Dusan Pekic, the secretary or the president of the lines of the veterans of the liberation war for Yugoslavia, would that mean anything to you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1058 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: So now I just reminded you that there was Dusan Pekic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1058 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Do you remember that General Dusan Pekic was a number one man in the association of Serbs from Croatia who assisted the Serbian autonomous provinces and sending volunteers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1058 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Did you know that General Dusan Pekic took from the military storehouses all the weapons that the JNA had planned to destroy and provided them to you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1058 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard something about it. I'm not quite sure how true that is.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And that is how the glorious partisan general Dusan Pekic and I, the nascent, the just-proclaimed Chetnik Vojvoda, found ourselves in a joint struggle, working on the reconciliation -- the national reconciliation of the Chetniks and the Partisans. Is this symbolic to you or is it not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1058 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It could be.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Do you know that the JNA, a year before that, took the weapons of all the Territorial Defences of the republics and provinces and put them in its depots?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1058 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is something I found out later.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Do you know that there were many obsolete pieces of weaponry there, carbines, 48; Thompson, American automatic rifles; and Spagin, the Russian type of automatic rifles; M-56s, and similar obsolete pieces of weaponry?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1058 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That -- those weapons were distributed to the volunteers as the primary type of weapon because there was no other type at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: This was distributed to you at the time when the JNA was not yet participating in combat?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1058 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: But we provided those weapons next to General Dusan Pekic. I never wanted to mention his name in public and here at the Tribunal while General Pekic was alive. Did you ever hear me mention his name?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1058 [Resumed]
utterances.text: To be sincere, I did not follow the proceedings of this Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: General Pekic died two years ago, and now I can candidly speak about this without inflicting any harm on him. Because this Western regime can no longer arrest him. That is obvious, is it not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1058 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Tell me, when you were transferred to the Serbian villages in Eastern Slavonia, there was weapons already waiting for you there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1058 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Precisely of the type that I referred to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1058 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the Spagins, the Thompsons, and the M-56s, the Yugoslav butts, as they were called.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Do you remember that I often told journalists who were always talking me that we got those weapons from abroad through Hungary?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1058 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember. I was already there. We did not watch much TV at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And when Slobodan Milosevic decided to accept the Vance-Owen Plan and when we severely clashed with his regime, do you remember me telling that it was him and his police who gave us the weapons because I wanted to heckle him as much as possible?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1058 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not remember, believe me.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: As regards this secret where we got our weapons and how Dusan Pekic provided the armaments for us is something that I never told anybody, but now I can say it in public because this is a historic fact. And there was quite a lot of weaponry, was it not so?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1058 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Although it was obsolete?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1058 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: On the other hand, the Croats had the most sophisticated weaponry; is that true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1058 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Do you remember me saying at a press conference, it was on TV, how I shot an anti-tank rocket-thrower, the Hamdas [phoen] type, of German manufacture, which was the most modern anti-tank weapon at the time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1058 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot remember that now.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: This was seised by volunteers of the Serbian Radical Party in battles around Mirkovci, Kosta Carina, later, combatants there, have you heard about him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1058 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I have heard about him, but I never met him.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Okay we have clarified that. Now, you came to those villages, you said what villages those were, and there you were assigned to Territorial Defence units; right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1058 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Under the command of the local TO commanders and the more prominent volunteers themselves were appointed commanders or "komandirs" of certain units up to company level?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1058 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Srecko Radovanovic was one of those who were appointed to such a post --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The microphone is not on.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Some ranks were referred to that volunteers had. Do you know anything about this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1058 [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, from the beginning we actually addressed one another by ranks. You would be either a reserve commanding officer or junior lieutenant, and such.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Yesterday I gave you some three documents. I hope that you still have them. Or have they taken them from you? I would like to use again the Greater Serbia paper from July 2 -- 1997.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can the witness please be shown page 7.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: This is a paper of the Serbian Radical Party and the Serbian Chetnik Movement. At that time actually it was only of the Serbian Chetnik Movement. Can you see the front page?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1058 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Later this became the paper of the Serbian Radical Party. Now I should like to ask you to turn to page 7. This is a big feature story from Ravna Gora, where there was a celebration to mark the uprising day which was -- the uprising which was initiated in 1941 by the glorious general Draza Mihajlovic; you have heard of him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1058 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. What page did you say I should look at?

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Page 7. There at Ravna Gora was a big celebration where some 10.000 people had assembled. I delivered a passionate patriotic speech there, and then a proclamation of Vojvoda Momcilo Djujic was read out, which had been sent from America. Here you can see towards the end of page 7 this proclamation starts with the words, "Brothers, Serbs, sisters, Serbian women, Serbian chosen people ..." Did you see that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1058 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Now, go to page 8. Here you see a photograph of Vojvoda -- of Duke Momcilo Djujic, the proclamation continues. And this is marked in handwriting as page 11, but it should be page 9 in the newspaper. Have you found it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1058 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I have.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: All right. Towards the end of the first column, the second paragraph from the top, Vojvoda Djujic is speaking about the victory of the Serbian Chetniks in Borovo Selo and says in this paragraph -- actually, can you read it for yourself or shall I read it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1058 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It will be easier if you read it. I'm not sure I found it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: "For the success and courage demonstrated, I have decorated and promoted to the rank of Major Mr. Todosijevic, commander of Chetnik platoon; Mr. Denis Bareta, deputy commander to the rank of captain; and all the other courageous Chetnik combatants I have promoted to officer rank. The Serbian nation is grateful to them, and their names will remain inscribed in the glorious history of the Serbian Chetnik Movement." Did I read it correctly?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1058 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Is there a problem?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I waited a moment so you could understand that there is -- it takes time before what you say is translated. You must understand that. And we can't follow. If you think that it's no problem for everyone not to follow, fine, go on. But I can tell you that I as a Judge cannot follow because the interpreters are panting. They just can't catch up with you. You are going much too fast.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mrs. Lattanzi, I would really like you and your colleagues to follow me, but I have so much to say, so much information that I would like to present here, so I speed up quite unconsciously. I will try and avoid that, but it will again happen. I know myself only too well. What can I do? In any case, I'll try and slow down.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, please wait before you answer. At least your answers are shorter than the questions. So, Witness, please wait a while before you start answering. So wait for Mr. Seselj to be finished with his question, then wait a little while, and then we can have your answer; otherwise, we cannot hear your answer and we can't follow.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: The proclamation ends there and then Duke Djujic signs his name as the president of the dukedom council and the president of the Chetnik Movement in the free world; you see that at the end?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1058 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And now you see that there were certain occasions when ranks were distributed and that that was done by Duke Momcilo Djujic; however, those ranks were assigned only up to September 1991, until the moment when we reached an agreement about the inclusion of the volunteers of the Serbian Radical Party directly into the units of the Yugoslav People's Army. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1058 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: When the Yugoslav People's Army engaged in combat and we joined them, then their rules applied to all of us; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1058 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: I don't remember a single case of anybody having been given a rank outside of the JNA after September 1991. There may have been such occasions, but I don't remember any such occasions, do you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1058 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: You do or you don't?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1058 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Very well. You automatically said "yes," so -- anyway. We have resolved this issue. Do you know that sometime in 1991 there was a clash between myself and Duke Djujic, that the two of us clashed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1058 [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that time, I was in a theatre of war, so --

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Did you hear that the things that did not function as they should have, even later?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1058 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: If I told you that we clashed because Duke Momcilo Djujic had sent me Dr. Milos Prica as my main political advisor and after my first contact with Dr. Prica I realised that he wanted me to provoke a civil war in Serbia and I rejected, I declined his services, and that was the reason why I clashed with Djujic. Do you know that? Does that tell you anything? Does this sound like a credible explanation for my clash with Duke Djujic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1058 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Did you hear that after that Duke Djujic sent the same person, Milos Prica from America to Biljana Plavsic and that he made Biljana Plavsic to become a traitor of the Serbian people; does that mean anything to you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1058 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Do you know that the same Milos Prica is the ambassador of Bosnia and Herzegovina in New York?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1058 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Very well. We have said that for the Trial Chamber, the general public who follow the trial, and the OTP. Now they know. Okay, you were now in Eastern Slavonia, the combat is ongoing, and fighting stops in November; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1058 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: A large number of volunteers returned after that to Serbia; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1058 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: You, Srecko Radovanovic, and a certain number of others who had made your name there as capable men found jobs in the police as far as I understand; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1058 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: We sent volunteers to defend the Serbian autonomous province, Eastern Slavonia, Baranja, and Srem; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1058 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: In addition to that, in the territory of the Croatian federal unit, there was the Serbian Autonomous Province of Western Slavonia and Krajina; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1058 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you're right.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: The three Serbian autonomous provinces were established in order to prevent Croatian separatism; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1058 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And the Serbs insisted on the preservation of those autonomous -- for the future in order to prevent any future Croatian separatist attempts; is that correct? However, despite of that, after the Vance Plan, Croatia was recognised as an independent state; then the Serbs decided to unite those three autonomous provinces into the Republic of Serbian Krajina because they concluded if Croatia was to secede from Yugoslavia, they would secede from Croatia; is that correct.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1058 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: It was only after the end of combat and fighting and after the implementation of the Vance-Owen Plan and after the international recognition of the independence of the Croatian state, the Republic of Serbian Krajina was established, it was only then; am I right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1058 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: The establishment of the Serbian Republic of Serbian Krajina was the consequence of Croatian separatism and not something that preceded Croatian separatism; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1058 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: So that move was imposed upon the Serbian people; it was not their struggle for a Greater Serbia; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1058 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Since you worked as a police officer for a time, you were selected as the best to go for training in Pajzos; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1058 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The microphone is not on.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: I remember that Srecko Radovanovic called me on the telephone and consulted me, asking me whether to go or not, and I told him to make his own decision. I did not have anything against it. It was the JNA who wanted you, it is to your honour, but you have to decide yourself. You didn't consult anybody. You accepted the invitation immediately; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1058 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: When you worked as a policeman in Eastern Slavonia, you carried police ID cards, you were professional policemen?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1058 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and we were paid by the police.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: When you arrived in Pajzos, did you keep the police documentation of the Serbian Republic of Krajina?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1058 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Were you given some other IDs?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1058 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, later.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: What IDs were you given?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1058 [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were given Serbian IDs.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: From Serbia?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1058 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Do you have that ID? Did you keep it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1058 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I returned it when I was wounded.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: I find it very strange that you were provided with IDs of the Republic of Serbia. Where is Pajzos?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1058 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Vojvodina.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: I have to correct you. Pajzos is near Ilok in the Republic of Serbian Krajina. It is currently the territory under Croatian occupation. It was never in Vojvodina.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1058 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I apologise. I was absolutely convinced that it was in Vojvodina.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Pajzos is in Ilok in the Republic of Serbian Krajina, which is currently the territory under Croatian control?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1058 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that it is near Ilok, but I thought it was Vojvodina. I was there only once for those few days.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: But then maybe this is a mistake. How come you were provided with Serbian mistake -- with Serbian ID in Pajzos?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1058 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it's not a mistake.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: When you left for Pajzos to go to Bosanski Samac, did you have military booklets?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1058 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And your participation in the fighting in Samac, was that recorded in your military booklet?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1058 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: So how could you join the 17th Tactical Group of the JNA if you didn't have a military booklet?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1058 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can I explain, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1058 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Whoever had a military booklet and the IDs that we had been provided with before our departure to Bosnia, we had to return all those and we received only platelets with ID numbers, like tags with ID numbers, and our first and family names.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Did you ever hear of Ilija Vuckovic, also known as Rambo?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1058 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Was he your commander in Pajzos?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1058 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was in Ilok --

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Hold on. He was the commander of the centre in Pajzos, near Ilok?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1058 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but his residence was in Ilok. He was the commander of both centres.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Yesterday you said that Franko Simatovic, Frenki, had been your commander?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1058 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Frenki was his commander. This one was the commander of the training centre, not my immediate superior.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: You perhaps do not know that I'm in the same unit with Franko Simatovic here in the Detention Unit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1058 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: He tells me that in Pajzos he was in Tito's villa in a radio interception centre.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1058 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he had his centre in Tito's villa, and why he was there is something I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: But you do know where the villa -- Tito's villa is?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1058 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do. That is the vineyard. It has houses, little sheds for labourers, where we were housed when we were there for training.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Was this villa separated from your training centre?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1058 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, some 100 or 200 metres uphill.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And he says that he met Srecko Radovanovic several times there, but they did not have any contacts along the line superior/subordinate?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1058 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not know what he says.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Let us see what Ilija Vuckovic says. He made a very short statement. This is document number one, I gave it to you yesterday. Can we have the usher give you that document, please, document number one.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: Would you be so kind as to give him document number one. Not mine, not mine.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Shall we look at it together, just the first two paragraphs of this statement. Have you gotten the statement?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1058 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I have received it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Ilija Vuckovic called Rambo says: "I was the operational commander of the unit for special purposes of the MUP of the Republic of Serbian Krajina." So this is a special purpose unit of the Republic of Serbian Krajina. Do you find anything odd there? "In the period from 1991 to the -- to March 1992, the seat of my unit was in Pajzos near Ilok in the Republic of Serbian Krajina." Did you see that paragraph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1058 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Is there anything strange there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1058 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what exactly you are referring to.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Do you know that he was the operational commander of the special purpose unit of the MUP of the Republic of Serbian Krajina in Pajzos near Ilok at that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1058 [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I knew things, he was the operational commander of the training centre, of that camp; as for other things, I really don't know, believe me.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: All right. In the second paragraph he says: "I remember that in March 1992 a group arrived for specialised training with members of the police of the Republic of Serbian Krajina. This group included Srecko Radovanovic, whom we called the fat one, Debeli. It did not have any party emblems and it was not a party unit because it consisted of members of different parties, and I did not ask anyone nor ask anyone to declare themselves as to party affiliation. The training was organised by the JNA, and I know that this group, having completed their training which was I believe in the first half of April 1992, together with members of the JNA, was transferred by JNA helicopters to Bosanski Samac." Are these facts true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1058 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but I think that this was the beginning of April. In the middle of April, on the 17th of April, Bosanski Samac was already taken.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: That is exactly what I say, in the first half of April.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1058 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Is everything that he says correct? You arrived in Samac by JNA helicopters and you joined the 17th Tactical Group under the command of Lieutenant-Colonel Stevo Nikolic, also known as Kriger; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1058 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not remember the name, and the surname I do remember the name.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: The nickname was Kriger --

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: I'm sorry, we now have a problem arising from the fact that we do not have an English version of the document that the accused is reading. But the accused put a proposition to the witness from this statement that he is now reading from, and the way the accused read out the statement, the facts that are described in the statement are dated as taking place in March 1992. So he's put a proposition about March 1992 to the witness, and I think that's important that it's on record that the date according to the witness statement that the accused is reading from is March. He's now having the witness put these facts in April. There's something strange about the way this statement is being used, because it seems to be describing events at another point in time.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There is no other reason in terms of time. They arrived for training in March. And in the beginning of April, they left Pajzos for Samac. So the temporal continuity is there, and it is quite logical.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Do you remember that you arrived for training in Pajzos in March or in some other month?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1058 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In March.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The witness is confirming that it was in March.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And in the statement that you gave to the OTP, do we have a date there at all? He shall take a look now to see when it was that you arrived in Pajzos for training. There is no reference to any time. The Prosecutor was not interested in finding that out when he took your statement. There is no time-framework at all about your arrival in Pajzos. They don't care. It is all the same to them because the Prosecutor can manipulate in this way; they can associate and correlate different events which are not associated necessarily, whereas Mr. Ilija Vuckovic's statement is quite precise, and you have confirmed its content, have you not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1058 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I have.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Well, now we are in Samac. In Samac while you were there when you arrived there in the 17th Tactical Group, was there at all a unit or any group of fighters who call themselves volunteers of the Serbian Radical Party, who identified themselves as such?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1058 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Here you have described in some detail the goings-on there, and I should like to find out from you another thing about this crime in Crkvina. Yesterday you steered clear of this subject, avoided to give us an answer, because Lugar has been dead for some time, for some years now. But we have to deal with this subject because even though Lugar is dead we cannot gloss over this fact. Actually, I didn't know myself about this crime until the time when Sulejman Tihic in December of last year actually confirmed that there had been exhumations and established that the crime had taken place. In your statement in paragraph 46 you say: "I saw Lugar and -- I saw Lugar and Tralja fire against these men killing five or seven of them ..." So you just heard the shooting; you did not see it personally. And then you go on to say: "I'm not sure if Debeli Musa also participated in the execution, but he was present ..."

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1058 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And yesterday, without any intervention on my part, you yourself said that Debeli Musa is not the same as Srecko Radovanovic, Debeli; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1058 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Well, now this is a very important question, and you have helped me much there for us to jointly unmask this OTP of the Tribunal at The Hague in terms of the methods that they employ.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, the witness does not have this, you have it. This is a summary of the statement of this witness of the 29th of March, 2007.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So that things are quite clear, this Debeli who's in Bosanski Samac is not the same person as the person named Debeli belonging to the Serbian Radical Party?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [Previous translation continues] ... in the same unit. There were two men by the same name, Debeli: Debeli, Srecko Radovanovic, the commander of the unit; and Debeli Musa, who was very fat. And that's why we also called him Debeli, fat. They were two different persons, but their nickname was the same.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As far as what happened in Bosanski Samac is concerned, it is Debeli Musa who was the person there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Both were in Bosanski Samac. In Crkvina it was only Debeli Musa who was there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Both were in Bosanski Samac --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- the one who was involved in the crime, was it Debeli Musa or the other Debeli?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Debeli Musa.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Where was Srecko in that time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I believe that he was in Bosanski Samac or perhaps in Pelagicevo. I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And now, Your Honours, I would like to draw your attention to the summary, together with the statement of the accused, provided on the 27th of -- 29th of March, 2007, on page 107 it is stated that the witness is going to talk about a group of volunteers, that's the penultimate paragraph, a group of volunteers of the SRS which was headed by Srecko Radovanovic, also known as Debeli. That group of SRS volunteers was trained for two weeks in a camp in Pajzos near Ilok. He will be talking about the training, instructors. And further on the witness will speak about the participation of volunteers in the events in Bosanski Samac, and he will describe the roles of Debeli --

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Your Honour, the accused is making submissions. He's not putting questions to the witness. He can make submissions in due course.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, this is a procedural remark. I believe that you need to know this. And we will also ask the witness to provide his comment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Put the question to the witness. The three Judges understand perfectly well and quickly. Please put the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: The question is this: Are you aware that the OTP manipulated with the fact provided by you and wanted to present to the Trial Chamber that the Debeli who was present during the killings committed by Lugar in Crkvina is the same Debeli whose real name is Srecko Radovanovic? And here I have a document which refers to Srecko Radovanovic, Debeli, his name is mentioned. And it is said in this document that you will be talking about the role of Debeli, and finally it says that: "The witness is going to testify about the killing of five to seven civilians in Crkvina by Lugar, Tralja, and another Chetnik, a volunteer. Debeli was there but the witness is not sure whether he participated in the killings." So there's no reference to Debeli Musa. There is just a continuity of the discourse, first Srecko Radovanovic Debeli, and then the conclusion. Are you area of the manipulation?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1058 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but I believe that I always drew a distinction between Debeli and Debeli Musa. If I say Debeli, I mean Srecko Radovanovic. If I say Debeli Musa, then it's Debeli Musa and nobody else, and it's a different person.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And you, Your Honours, I would like to remind you that I have publicly thanked a Muslim witness who was a victim to helped me to clarify that Srecko Radovanovic Debeli and the Debeli who was present during the crime were not one in the same person. Maybe you will remember this. I can maybe refer you to your services who can remind you of that part of the transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Mussemeyer, we have already heard a witness as regards this person Debeli, that's right. The Debeli that is mentioned in the 2007 statement may -- might not be Srecko Radovanovic, in the light of what the witness is telling us.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUSSEMEYER
utterances.text: Your Honours, I know this. I only wanted to correct for the record. It is not true that the Prosecution said it was Debeli Srecko Radovanovic. I quote directly from the witness statement. It is from the second -- the second statement of 2006, paragraph 46, there is written: "I am not sure if ... a.k.a. Debeli and then Musa also participated in the execution of these people, but he was present ..." So it is already said in the statement the OTP took from the witness. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is important. I thank you, Mr. Mussemeyer, to have told us --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- 2006 already. There was some hesitation --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [Previous translation continues] ... summary is not for me but for you, to convince you about the relevance of every witness. Look at the summary that refers to this witness dated 29th March, 2007. It is not in dispute that the OTP mixes up the Debeli who participated in the killing with Srecko Radovanovic Debeli. Please look at the summary and all shall become clear. This is not the first time that I am encountering such manipulation and traps set for me by the OTP. There is a lot of that, and I am the only one who had to deal with them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Seselj, there might be a misinterpretation, a mistake, confusion on the part of the Prosecution without there being an intention of forging or manipulating the truth. This is what you have concluded, but it might also be due to hesitations.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [Previous translation continues] ... then you can say that the indictment against me is also a mistake. The indictment is full of errors. Will you remember the meeting in Mali Zvornik that was located by them two years later than it actually happened? It's all full of mistakes. These proceedings are full of tricks by the OTP. Remember the witness 008? We still don't know whether he was at all capable of firing a fire-arm.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please proceed. You have approximately 30 minutes left.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Tell me, please, do you remember when Srecko Radovanovic left Samac?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1058 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't give you the exact date. I can tell you just approximately. In the meantime, he had gotten married, I believe in -- that was in August. I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Is it possible that already towards the end of May or the beginning of June he left Samac and then returned?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1058 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's a possibility. At that time I was in hospital, so I'm not sure. For 15, 20 days I was in hospital, so that is possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Something very strange happened when you left Samac, and the OTP helped me, and I'm very grateful to the Prosecutor, but they didn't do it on purpose. In any case, they helped me to clarify that matter. Something strange happened. Negotiations were conducted between the local authorities of Samac and a group of men who had already been there as members of the 17th Tactical Group of the JNA. They were asked to return and to fight for money in the territory of Samac. Do you know anything about that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1058 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about the money, but I know that there were talks to that event and that the late Lugar and some other man did return later on to the same area.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Did Lugar come back on his own initiative?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1058 [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, yes, he did.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And here we have a document issued by the Army of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, the OTP should provide you the document in the English because I don't carry anything in English, just in Serbian.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And in that document there is an analysis of the events in the territory of Samac. And a reference is made in one place -- let me just find that. Let me find the document, please. I'm so burdened that it is -- I'm encumbered with all these documents. Before I find this document, we shall take a look at what was shown by the OTP yesterday. That is this photostatic copy of a page from the paper "Svetlost" which is published in Kragujevac. It is P1041, if you can call it up on the screen, please.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Do we have it? Can we see it?

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: We have this report now, but leave that, we shall come back to that. Anyway, this is a report of the command of the 2nd Posavina Infantry Brigade in Samac.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please let us see this report also in the Serbian language, the one that we had just a while ago on the left side. Please return the document. It is document 1730 according to the 65 ter list. Is this -- is this waiting also going to be detracted from my time -- deducted from my time? The document, Judges, that you see on the right-hand side in English is what I want in Serbian on the left-hand side. Yes, here we have it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: This is a document of the command of the 2nd Posavina Infantry Brigade from Samac of the 1st of December, 1992. Are you able to see it? Do you see this? Do you see the heading of the document?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1058 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Fine. Turn to page 4, please. Here, a group of officers, 13 officers, the commander of the brigade Lieutenant-Colonel Mile Deronja, the Chief of Staff Captain Milan Jocic, and a whole series of other officers from this brigade are giving a report on developments in Samac and the bad relations between the Army of Republika Srpska and the local authorities in Samac. At the end of page 4 on the -- they say 9th, some developments which have been happening recently both within the 2nd Posavina Infantry Brigade as well as within the civilian authorities in the Samac municipality are nothing surprising for those who are well acquainted with the situation but have only surfaced the dirty laundry which has been collected in these areas for quite some time. We shall just point to some characteristic developments. Some members of the local authorities are contributing to the engagement of volunteers from Serbia, first under the control of Debeli, and later by -- the control of this is by Crni. Allegedly 50.000 German marks are allotted per member on condition that they conquer Orasje and that a rich war booty is found there. They promised this to over 700 volunteers. The first group included some 300, but in fact there were only 30 volunteers, some of whom who had never seen the theatre of war.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's comment: This was translated and not read from the English translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Have you seen this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1058 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I haven't seen any part of this text. Where should I look, at the screen or where?

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: You could only have seen it on the screen and nowhere else. What does this tell us now? It tells that the local authorities first planned Srecko Radovanovic, and when he refused then they talked to Crni, that is, Dragan Djordjevic Crni; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1058 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And the army informed the superior command of the Army of Republika Srpska that the local authorities were negotiating with some who were volunteers earlier to come and to bring others, and they were promised 700 volunteers and that the first group would have 300, whereas only 30 showed up. Someone had planned to attack Orasje. Do you know where Orasje is?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1058 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: There was a front line between Samac and Orasje?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1058 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Orasje was held by the Croats; right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1058 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Someone from the local authorities planned an attack on Orasje and was offering money for the engagement of these volunteers; is that clear from the text which I read out?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1058 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Can this have any connection with the Serbian Radical Party, this private arrangement?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1058 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Was this the reason for Lugar to again return to Samac?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1058 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Possibly. I cannot give you a full response.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: But are you familiar with the fact that after all of you left Samac, after all of you had left Samac, he of his own accord returned to Samac with a group of people?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1058 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: We are again assisted by this OTP document, that is, "Svetlost," of the 13th of August, 1998.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now see that on the ELMO? I indicated the document's number a while ago. I'm lost in all these papers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could you give the number of the document of August 13, 1998?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It was admitted yesterday. The number P1041. You admitted it as an exhibit of the OTP yesterday, although actually the OTP withheld one paragraph from you. Perhaps you will recall that I intervened on that account.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Mussemeyer.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUSSEMEYER
utterances.text: If I may, it was the document with the 65 ter number 7530 that has the document identification 0341-7948.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Please look at page 2 of this document. This Article was published after Lugar had been killed. You heard that Lugar had been killed in Kragujevac?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1058 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: He had a personal conflict with a local member of the State Security Service, and this latter guy shot him; did you hear about that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1058 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did. I read about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: After Lugar was killed, the Kragujevac paper "Svetlost" published this article, and the last paragraph in the first column of this says -- can you look at it? I am going to read it out and you can follow the text on the screen. The first -- the last, actually, paragraph of the first column. I can have it zoomed in for you.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1058 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: "The unit which was led by Slobodan Miljkovic Lugar was a part of the volunteers sent to Croatia and Bosnia by the Serbian Radical Party from Kragujevac." This is what the journalist is saying. And then he goes on: "The then-president of the municipal board of the Serbian Radical Party Tomislav Nikolic denied stories that the Radicals had organised the transfer of Miljko's volunteers across the border of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia. The group referred to had gone to theatres of war earlier as well in Baranja, Western Srem, Slavonia, and Bosnia. This time they went of their own initiative because they considered to have -- to be -- have a great obligation towards those people there, the people there, even though I drew attention to them that now our authorities can easily have them arrested." Did I read this correctly?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1058 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: So Tomislav Nikolic is confirming that the second time they went there it was of their own initiative?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1058 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: That autumn you were arrested in Samac and taken to Banja Luka; right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1058 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: You, Lugar, and another number of people were arrested?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1058 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The entire unit plus me.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And that entire unit, did it have anything to do with the Serbian Radical Party at that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1058 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, none whatsoever.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: You were arrested because there had been a clash between you and some scouting detachment; am I right -- of some other Serbian unit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1058 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: You tried to disarm that other unit, they put up resistance, and on that occasion a member of that unit was killed; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1058 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And then you were arrested but then you were set free because there was no evidence against you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1058 [Resumed]
utterances.text: After the first interview with the investigating judge, we were set free.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Very well. And the OTP found in a book of mine which has been submitted as 1965 according to 65 ter list. It was my show broadcast on Radio Kragujevac on the 28th November, 1993. And in that show, it was a phone-in show. People phoned in and asked me questions. One of the questions was this: Why I, as the president of the party, did not intervene when Lugar and his group of men were arrested in Samac and taken to Banja Luka? And the question was put to me about Grey Wolves. I'm showing here that I don't have a clue what this was all about, that as a matter of fact I mistook the Grey Wolves for Wolves from Vucak. Do you hear of wolves from Vucak?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1058 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: That was a unit from the vicinity of Banja Luka?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1058 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And they didn't have anything to do with the Grey Wolves; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1058 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And in that show I didn't know what they would ask me, and I said that I don't know -- I haven't a clue that they had ever been there, that there were armed members there, and that they were ever arrested --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And I suppose, Your Honours, that you have this in this English language and it has been translated so I will no longer linger upon this. And I explain here what my relationship with Arkan was. And if I have some more time -- can you please tell me how much more time do I have at the moment?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I believe that you have 15 minutes left now.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. I will make the most of the 15 minutes that I'm left to clarify the relationship between volunteers of the Serbian Radical Party and Arkan's men, although I have pointed to the document where I explained that very well in a radio show.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: We have mentioned here that in Prigrevica, in the training centre, there were also members of other parties; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1058 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: However, there was no single Arkan's man there; right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1058 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Arkan had his own training centres, he had his own facilities, and so on and so forth; right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1058 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you're right.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Did it happen that our volunteer at a certain stage joined Arkan's unit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1058 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it did happen a few times.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: What in your view was so attractive in Arkan's unit for those men to join them? Not many did, five or six, but they did?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1058 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Believe me, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Did you hear that Arkan paid his men a lot of money?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1058 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I heard that, if that's what you meant.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Do you know that they had the best equipment, the best weapons?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1058 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that. I saw that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And do you know that Arkan also looted the areas of combat?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1058 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Do you know that a lot of criminal affairs were tied to Arkan's name?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1058 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: A certain number of men cared about the huge pay in Arkan's unit, and that's why they joined them having left our volunteer groups; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1058 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: It happened that two men joined Arkan's unit as early as September 1991. I'm not too sure that there were two. Yesterday, the OTP showed you a video-clip from the funeral of a man who was a volunteer of the Serbian Radical Party, and they mispronounced his name. First they said that he was Slobodan Jovic and then Slobodan Jojic, and so on. Actually, it was Slobodan Jocic. Did you ever hear of Slobodan Jocic? On the 4th [as interpreted] of September he was killed in Laslovo.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1058 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, together with three other men.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: At the time when he was killed, was he a member of our volunteer unit or was he a member of Arkan's men?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1058 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, he was a member of Arkan's unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Do you know that before he was our volunteer?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1058 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And then he joined Arkan's unit and he was killed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1058 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you're right.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And the journalist says it's very clearly that he was a member of the Serbian Radical Party, but that he was Arkan's fighter; did we hear that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1058 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: It was similar with Mirko Lovadinovic who was killed on the same day, I believe, on the 14th of September?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1058 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the two of them were in the group of four, and they were killed on the same day.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: In Laslovo?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1058 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And Mirko Lovadinovic, who was a university professor, he worked at the school for [indiscernible]; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1058 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I believe so.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: According to my information, he was with our volunteers until his group returned to Serbia?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1058 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he was with our volunteers, and I believe that he was billeted in the village called Ada.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And when his group returned to Serbia, he decided to stay on and continue fighting and that's why he joined Arkan's men?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1058 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is possible. At that time, I was already in a different village.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And he died in fighting? The Croats shot him from a small-calibre rifle?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1058 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe so, but I'm -- can't remember the details.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: I saw photos from the post mortem. Half of his head was missing as a result of that shot. Do you know that small-calibre weapons are forbidden according to the rules of war?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1058 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Because a small-calibre bullet causes the so-called inhumane wounds; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1058 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: If you're hit in the head, then it destroys half of the head; if it hits you in the body, then the bullet travels and damages many of the internal organs; am I right? This is a layman's interpretation?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1058 [Resumed]
utterances.text: You're absolutely right.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: So he was hit with the forbidden bullets. Do you know that anybody on the Serbian side used forbidden weapons and bullets in the war?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1058 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Did you also hear that Croats used sub-calibre automatic weapons of Singapore make?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1058 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, SA-80.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And the bullet of those Singapore weapons, do they cause the same consequences?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1058 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, their calibre is 5.56, a small calibre.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Do you also know that the Croats engaged Kurdish mercenaries in the fighting in Eastern Slavonia?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1058 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Were there any fallen Kurds in the fighting that you participated in --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, it seems that you are well versed in ballistics, but I'm a bit surprised by Mr. Seselj's logic, which you proved. He says that small-calibre weapons are banned by international texts. Calibre 5.56 is what the French army has at the moment, I believe, and other armies also. So could you expand on this a little?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I absolutely agree with you. The French M-16 -- I apologise, the French M-2000 and the American M-16 and the British SA-80, and the Russian Kalashnikov AK-74 [as interpreted]; they all use a 5.56 calibre which is forbidden according to the Geneva Conventions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. We'll check that. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Presiding Judge, the JNA never had such weapons, never.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Am I right when I say this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1058 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] How much time do I still have? Can you please tell me?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
