utterances.text: Fine. But I would like to know something else. Were all those whom you considered members of the Serbian Chetnik Movement members of the Serbian Radical Party or of its section called the Serbian Chetnik Movement?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1058 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Seselj, I'm trying to understand you. The only people that I -- the only one who I know about at the time was Mirko Blagojevic from Bijeljina. He belonged to the Serbian Chetnik Movement, and he was a duke, a Vojvoda as you are yourself aware.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: All right. Did you ever hear that there was a Serbian Radical Party in Brcko when you were there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1058 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not see it established formally, but I did know a gentleman. I perhaps was even friends with him before the war. He himself said that he was a member of the Serbian Radical Party in Brcko. That's what he said. I don't know whether it was actually so.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: I never heard that we had a Serbian Radical Party there before the war. We did have one in Bijeljina, but not in Brcko. In Brcko it was only in 1994 that we formed one.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1058 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that you are right there, but I can tell you this: One of the sympathisers as the man himself said of the party I knew and he said that he was a member of the Serbian Radical Party.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: All right. You gave a number of statements about what you had experienced in Brcko in May 1992 and at the beginning of June; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1058 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: You gave a statement to the Danish Helsinki Committee on the 25th of May, 1993; do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1058 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: There you described numerous crimes, but in just one place you say that Mirko Blagojevic from Bijeljina, with his Chetniks, was in Brcko. You do not ascribe a single crime or anything bad to him. And when you described the crimes, you attribute them to Arkan's men, to Mauzer; and now do you mention here Goran Jelesic? I'm not quite sure. I cannot look for it now. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1058 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. As I told you before, when the Trial Chamber asked me and when Mr. Prosecutor asked me, all that I saw Mirko Blagojevic and his men do was the incident which happened when he delivered us this speech at Luka. I was not affected then and when they beat up the other prisoners.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: I have read all your statements. It was the first time today that you say that Mirko Blagojevic brought biscuits and cigarettes, treated you to these there. This is never mentioned in any of your previous statements in these -- all these cases that you testified in.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1058 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is mentioned, Mr. Seselj. It is.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Let us wager a bet here. If this is proven by the Prosecutor, I will confess to all the crimes that I'm charged with and I also -- I challenge Mr. Mussemeyer to this. So when you were talking with the Danish Helsinki Committee, you never mentioned anything bad that could be attributed to Mirko Blagojevic. We agree there, right? Before this statement that you gave to the Danish Helsinki Committee in 1992 --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Have you found it, Mr. Mussemeyer?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUSSEMEYER
utterances.text: No, I don't refer to this. But I wanted to remind you that the witness in his statement he gave to the OTP says related to the statement he gave to the Danish Helsinki Committee --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Don't remind us of that. You had ample time. We'll come to that, Mr. Mussemeyer. You don't have the right to do this --

utterances.speaker: MR. MUSSEMEYER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... use this, then, because the witness said --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm using everything that is useful to me. Don't ask me why I used this. I can use whatever. I am very sovereign in my defence, and only the Trial Chamber can put objections of this nature to me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Mussemeyer, what are the grounds for your objection, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUSSEMEYER
utterances.text: Because the witness said in his statement he gave to the OTP and it is in number 1: "I must point out that many facts in the record of this interview," referring to the interview to the Danish Helsinki Committee, "are incorrect due to the fact and the fact that I never signed that record since I received a copy of it in English a long time after the interview was held. I do not consider it to be my statement." And that should be on the record. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, we should look at the record to see that it is a trick by the OTP against Frederick Harhoff. They put it in the statement, and they gave it to the witness to sign. Discrepancy between the statement given to the Danish Helsinki Committee and the first statement given to the OTP consist only in the numbers of killed, but the OTP is trying to influence Mr. Harhoff so as to make Mr. Harhoff take a negative stance towards me. Sometimes Mr. Harhoff is aware of that, sometimes he is not. And what Mr. Mussemeyer is doing is absolutely pointless, although he's the best Prosecutor in this OTP.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Witness, do you remember that the statement you provided to the Danish Helsinki Committee already in 1992, before that you provided a statement to the military security service of the JNA?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1058 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Never. I never provided a statement to the military security -- military security service of the JNA.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: That statement is on two pages?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1058 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The only thing is that I made a record that Captain Dragan insisted on.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Okay, okay. Let's take it easy. That statement got into the hands of the military security services?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1058 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: As your statement, which you signed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1058 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't sign anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: How come you didn't sign it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1058 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The man never asked me to sign it, Mr. Seselj.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: First of all, you said --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Slowly. Please slow down. Please slow down.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Your Honours, I am on my feet because I am informed that the accused is in the -- that the witness is using his first name when he is answering questions, and it doesn't reflect in the English translation. So I don't know how quite we deal with this, but it seems that we may need a redaction of the B/C/S version of the live feed from the court today.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I didn't hear that, but they are doing it on purpose in order to disturb the transmission. I am interested in public trial, not in a private trial. You said that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Seselj, Mr. Seselj, you should not mention the first name of the witness. It seems that --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, never. I did not. Although Mr. Mussemeyer is the best Prosecutor and sometimes he makes a mistake of this sort, I'm a bit younger by at least 30 years and such mistakes never happen to me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You did not enter this first name?

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Tell me this, is it true --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I proceed?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, did you say your first name? Did you mention your first name? Can you confirm this?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Let's redact this then. Thank you. Mr. Seselj, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to say that this is what the Prosecutor said. He said exactly that. He never said that the accused had said anything. He said the witness pronounced his own name, his first name. That's all he said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. My fellow Judge Lattanzi is absolutely right. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Oh, very well, I've been exculpated.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Is it true that when you were interviewed on that occasion and that that was recorded there, you said that nobody had beaten you personally and that everything [as interpreted] treated you fairly? Is that what you stated and was that recorded?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1058 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did say that I had been beaten, but it was not recorded.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: So you said that you had been beaten but that was not recorded?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1058 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I was beaten.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Okay. You're saying that you were beaten. But when you spoke to them, did you tell them that you had been beaten?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1058 [Resumed]
utterances.text: With whom, Mr. Seselj?

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: You say with Captain Dragan. What was the name of the other officer who was with you who took you to Captain Dragan?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1058 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Rade Bozic.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Rade Bozic, was he present when that record was made?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1058 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Only Captain Dragan was there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1058 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: In what capacity did he make that record, who was he then? That was in Zvornik?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1058 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Where was it then?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1058 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Belgrade on the 13th floor of the Beogradjanka building.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Why did you go to him there?

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Who brought you from Zvornik to him, to Serbia?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUSSEMEYER
utterances.text: I think --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We need another redaction, line 23, page 98. I beg you both to slow down. Slow down. You are speaking much too fast. You think we know your language perfectly, but that's the problem; we don't, unfortunately. It takes time to learn this language.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Who took you to Captain Dragan?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1058 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Rade Bozic took me from Luka, and I met Captain Dragan on that same day in Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: But I just said that it was in Zvornik and you said, No, not in Zvornik, in Beogradjanka. You met Captain Dragan in Zvornik, and Captain Dragan allegedly personally took you to Belgrade; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1058 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. He did not personally take me, but we shared the same vehicle and a journalist of illustrated politics. And Rade Bozic was also in the same car. And that's when, together with them, I went to Belgrade, or rather, to Zemun to the golden oar restaurant where my wife was waiting for me with some friends.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Did you provide this statement in the golden oar?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1058 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, two days later I met Captain Dragan, and then he said, Come to me to Beogradjanka building.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Did you tell him that you had been beaten?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1058 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: So how come that wasn't recorded?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1058 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know, Mr. Seselj.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Very well then. And why didn't you say to Mr. Harhoff and the Danish Helsinki Committee anything about Mirko Blagojevic and the alleged Radicals who had ill treated the prisoners?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1058 [Resumed]
utterances.text: One more thing, Mr. Seselj, Mr. Prosecutor here is right. Not only in the statement that you have was it where I distanced myself from that testimony, but in my four previous testimonies I repeated every time that I did not sign the statement that was compiled at the Danish Helsinki Committee.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Okay. Let's move on. There is a statement that you did sign. On the 4th and 5th of April, 1995, you spoke to the Prosecutors of The Hague Tribunal, and you provided a statement on a total of 13 pages, and you signed that statement in 1995. In that statement - I'm looking at it - on the 13 pages of this statement you don't mention Mirko Blagojevic or his Chetniks. Nowhere in this big huge statement. You only mentioned a Chetnik by the name of Enver, who carved a cross on Ibrahim Mulagovic's [phoen] forehead. You don't say that he had anything to do with Mirko Blagojevic. You don't mention Mirko Blagojevic. You don't mention the Serbian Radical Party or my name. This is your statement provided to The Hague Tribunal in 1995. The Trial Chamber has it, the OTP has it, and you signed it. Where is Mirko Blagojevic in there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1058 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you're right, I did sign it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: But no Mirko Blagojevic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1058 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can I tell you why Mirko Blagojevic is not there?

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Go on, then.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1058 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mirko Blagojevic did not beat me personally. Chetniks didn't beat me. I never said that. When people ask me things, I answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: But you did not provide the statement only about who beat you. You also provided a statement about who beat the others, who ill treated the prisoners, who killed the prisoners. And you told everything in the statement. But in the entire statement, there is no reference to Mirko Blagojevic, the Serbian Radical Party, or the Serbian Chetnik Movement. In the entire statement nowhere do I find those things.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1058 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I agree, you are absolutely right. Which doesn't mean that what I have just said today before the Trial Chamber, before the OTP, and before you is not correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: I'm not interested in that. I'm not interested whether it's correct or not. I want to speak the language of facts.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1058 [Resumed]
utterances.text: You're right.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: You have -- go on and try to convince somebody else, not me.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1058 [Resumed]
utterances.text: You're absolutely right, Mr. Seselj. I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: I'm not here to commend you. I'm here to refute your testimony.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1058 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And I'm using all the weapons that I have at my disposal to refute your testimony.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1058 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I agree with you, Mr. Seselj.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: In the record, Captain Dragan's record, there is nothing about it. In your statement to the Danish Helsinki Committee there is nothing about it, but there is a reference, one reference, that Mirko Blagojevic was in Brcko. In your 1995 statement to the OTP investigators, not a single reference to it. On the 15th of May, 1996, you gave The Hague investigators a supplementary statement. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1058 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they asked me about that statement, Mr. Seselj. I never signed it. I did talk to the investigators in connection with that statement, and I said if they wanted to speak more about it we could do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Whether you signed it or not, this is something I won't go into it.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1058 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: But, however, the OTP at The Hague submitted this to me as a supplement to your statement.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1058 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would sign it right now in front of you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Do not sign anything in front of me, please do not sign, for heaven's sake, my papers.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1058 [Resumed]
utterances.text: You are quite right, Mr. Seselj.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: In this supplement, you never make any reference to either Mirko Blagojevic or to the Serbian Radical Party or to me or to the Radicals or to the Serbian Chetnik Movement; in no place do you make any such reference?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1058 [Resumed]
utterances.text: You are quite right.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Then we have 2008, well into my trial, in other words, The Hague OTP calls you, and the OTP at The Hague prepares in advance a statement for you to sign; right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1058 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that they prepared any statement in advance for that purpose.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: In 2008, that was on the 11th of December, 2008, do you remember that encounter?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1058 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not have a contact then. I received this document, this statement that I was supposed to read, and to sign every page of that statement, you're right.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: How did you get it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1058 [Resumed]
utterances.text: By mail.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: The OTP at The Hague prepared this statement, sent it to you by post, and you signed every page and then sent it back?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1058 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you are quite right.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Gentlemen of the Trial Chamber, Judges, I hope that you heard this. This statement under 92 bis was drawn up by the OTP, sent to the witness by mail for him to sign every page and to send it back. This is what the witness has just said.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, to read it, and if I agreed with everything in it, to sign the way you have described it. And I did say that I would do so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, this is important. You're saying -- you're telling us - and you're under oath - that you received a statement dated 11 December 2008 sent by mail. Was it written in English or in your own language? In English obviously?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In Bosnian Serbo-Croat, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [Previous translation continues] ... language, in your own language, several pages long, you read it and signed it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. And certified by a notary public. This is what the officer of the Tribunal, the employee of the Tribunal, said I should do. And I did so. I had it thus authenticated.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We have this authentication by a public -- notary public in a city in a foreign country in which this witness probably lives. I shall not mention the name.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This has never happened in any trial as far as I know, namely, that the OTP prepared a so-called consolidated statement under Rule 92 bis and sent it by mail without any conversation, without any consultations, without any consideration to the witness, with the annotation: If you agree, sign it and send it back. And a while ago the Prosecutor wanted you to admit this into the file. Now, the first thing in the statement --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just a minute. Witness, it seems that this statement is different from what you said earlier on a number of points. So why did you sign it? You could have disagreed with it. You could have not signed it.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Judge, sir, I probably supplemented it by describing this incident in Luka when Mirko Blagojevic's men came. I have given so many statements that -- and I believe that I described this orally many times here in the courtroom. And I stand behind what I signed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, if I understand you correctly, you testified before the Helsinki Commission and did not mention Mirko Blagojevic or anything of the sort. Then later you were interviewed by Captain Dragan and there was another statement but you don't mention it. And in 2008 suddenly we have a statement with other elements. Is this what happened?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As regards the statement to the Helsinki Committee, I did have a conversation with them, an interview with them, and Mr. Harhoff was present. I talked with Mr. Sisby, and Mr. Harhoff was with my wife outside that office. He was not present at all when I was having this interview with a so-called interpreter. She could not speak either good English -- Bosnian, Serbo-Croat, or Danish. I asked after the conversation, Should I sign anything? And they told me, This is not a document for any signature, any sign. If need be I shall send you the document. After a certain time, I got that document in English. I regret the fact that I do not have these copies, because I tried to rectify the things which I then understood. As regards the statement to Captain Dragan, I tell you that was done in his office, and I don't (redacted)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We need another redaction, Mr. Registrar. Very well. I see that we're running out of time.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am in a panic as to whether I shall have enough time. How much time do I have left ?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We still have 20 minutes before 7.00, and I don't know how much time you have left. I'll tell you in a minute. 10 to 15 minutes -- 12 minutes. I was right. 12 minutes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Little time, very little time.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Now, look here. You are far away. The OTP is here at The Hague. The OTP does its work and discharges conscientiously its duty because they are conscientious and honourable men. But the OTP has a need in this trial which it is conducting against me. They put their need on paper without you in your absence and they send it to you and they tell you, Read this and sign it if you agree. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1058 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Now, without you, without having talked to you, the OTP in the first paragraph actually swoops upon Mr. Harhoff and says that many facts in the record from the statement to the Danish Helsinki Committee are incorrect. And they send this to you. And now you receive it, how carefully you read it - I will not go into that, maybe you did, maybe you didn't. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1058 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that is not exactly the way it was, Mr. Seselj.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Anyway, you signed it and you sent it to the OTP. And the OTP is now proposing this to be directly admitted into the file under 92 ter. Fortunately, the Trial Chamber did not admit it.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Think, Judges, how many other things have already been admitted under this rule in this way -- well, anyway. This is a finished thing. It is a done thing.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Now, the OTP introduces Mirko Blagojevic for the first time in the penultimate paragraph, that is, paragraph 42 --

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Sorry, Your Honours, the witness should be allowed to explain how it actually was that the statement was made. The accused put a proposition to him and the witness say, No, that is not how it was.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't have the time for that. Let somebody else ask that. The OTP should have done that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: On the 22nd of October, 2009, you provided a new statement. You added some things. But, again, you never mentioned either Mirko Blagojevic or myself or the Serbian Radical Party. You did mention a Chetnik flag that you saw somewhere, but that is neither here nor there. Sir, these are all your statements that you provided to The Hague OTP. I have read your testimonies in the four previous cases. Can I publicly say which cases those all were? Because you were not protected in those case and you are protected here. May I mention them? Maybe it will reveal his identity. Am I allowed?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let's move into closed session.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no, then I give up.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: No, no. I'm not going to ask you about what you said --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Mussemeyer.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUSSEMEYER
utterances.text: I'm terribly sorry to interrupt, but Mr. Seselj said that it was in this statement that the witness the first time mentioned Mirko Blagojevic. If you look carefully at paragraph 32, every time when he mentioned Mirko Blagojevic there is at the end of the sentence the source when he mentioned it the first time. And he mentioned Mirko Blagojevic already in testimonies in other trials. So it's quite possible that the first time in the statement he mentioned him because his statements from before were from 1995, but in the meantime the witness has testified at least three times in other cases, and there he mentioned Mirko Blagojevic. You can check this every time when you check the source given in paragraph 42. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not true what Mr. Mussemeyer is saying is not true. Look at paragraph 42, Your Honours. It says about Mirko Blagojevic. Him and his escorts introduced themselves as Serbian Chetniks and Radicals. And after that there is a reference. On the 4th of February, 2004, in one case on page 477. And then his men arrived in the camp several times and ill treated and beat the prisoners. You won't find that in none of the four testimonies, and there's not even a reference like in paragraph 42. This is a lie, and this is the OTP's trick. Maybe Mr. Mussemeyer doesn't know that because he is a very capable OTP, but somebody else may have plotted this. You won't find that in none of the four testimonies. And I don't want to move into a private session --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Seselj, that is enough.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Do you want me to stop? Okay, I'll stop.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You have understood what I am saying, to always talk about the Prosecutor, whether he's good or bad, you are making fun of us.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mrs. Lattanzi, I have established some things and I would like to pin-point them. And I would like to make the strongest possible impression on the general public because I believe that this is the fundamental part of these proceedings, what has just happened --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Seselj, you are talking to a judicial Bench, not to the public at large. We are not making speeches to the public at large here.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mrs. Lattanzi, I am addressing you, the Trial Chamber, and I am also addressing the general public because you are trying me and the general public is trying you. And it is not enough for justice to be administered here. The general public has to gain the impression that justice is indeed administered here. And I would like to remind you of this principle. You are trying me, the general public is trying you. Who is going to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We are very familiar with that principle. I shall not respond anymore because we are in a hurry.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Okay. I have very little time. Can you remember very precisely when was it that Mirko Blagojevic came to the Luka camp?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1058 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let's say that it was on the 29th or the 30th of May.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: The 29th or the 30th of May?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1058 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: On what occasion?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1058 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Did you hear that a member of his unit, Branislav Filipovic, Sumar, was killed in the month of May during the battle for Brcko?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1058 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I heard it from the local Serbs who worked with me.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: When did that happen? Can you be very precise?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1058 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard that it was on the 15th or the 17th of May. I don't know exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: The dead body of Branislav Filipovic, Sumar, remained on the Muslim side; the Muslims got hold of his dead body; right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1058 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Do you know that his dead body was exchanged?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1058 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Let's look at the document --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Seselj, not today but at a later stage I would like the Prosecutor to tell me why the stamp of the notary public of a state I shall not mention is dated the 24th of March, 2010. I would like someone to explain this to me, why it says 24th of March, 2010. I would like a very accurate explanation for this. That said, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone not on.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And now could the usher please put a very short document on the ELMO, or, rather, put it to the witness. This is Mirko Blagojevic's statement. The OTP and the Trial Chamber already have it. This is Mirko Blagojevic's statement. It's very short.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Would you please be so kind and read it aloud.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1058 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The whole statement?

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: It's not long.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1058 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: If you are up to it; if not, I can read it.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1058 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can do it. "I Mirko Blagojevic born on the 1st of August, 1956" --

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: You can skip the personal data. Let's go to the statement itself.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1058 [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Statement, the company which I commanded was called the Serbian Chetnik detachment and was part of the Territorial Defence at the SAO of Semberija and Majevica. We participated in the fighting for the liberation of Brcko from the 3rd to the 17th of May, 1992. My unit participated in breaking through the corridor towards Obudovac and consolidating positions at the sector of Ivici as well as the expansion of liberated territory at the sector of Klanac and the stretch of the shoe factory Izvor. The unit had about 100 people. Most of the people in the unit were members of the Serbian Radical Party from Bijeljina, and there were some from other parties as well as those who were not members of any party. But at that time it did not matter at all who came from which party. What was primary was the struggle, and the Chetnik Movement is the common tradition of the entire Serbian people. "In my unit there was not a single volunteer from Serbia. We returned from Brcko on the 17th of May because there was a certain truce and there was also a conflict between me and Ljubisa Savic, Mauzer, which went back to the time of the liberation of Bijeljina. Mauzer was a member of Arkan's volunteer guard, and we could not -- we just could not agree on participation in concerted actions, and that is why, in order to avoid an armed clash between our units in agreement with the command of the Territorial Defence, we decided to go back to Bijeljina. "I was at the Luka camp only once on the 16th of May, 1992. Namely, a member of my unit Filipovic Branislav called Sumar was killed in Brcko and the Muslims got hold of his dead body and asked 20 of their own in exchange. With the Muslim side by radio communications, we agreed on this exchange. I addressed the town command, and the command decided that 20 Muslim prisoners should be taken over from the Luka camp and the -- handed over to the Muslim side and that the Muslim side should deliver the dead body of our killed combatant. "We returned to Brcko on the 12th of June, 1992, at the invitation of the Army of Republika Srpska, i.e., at the call of Captain Seho vac. Then they assigned us in such a way that we could not have any contact with" --

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Ljubisa Savic, Mauzer.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1058 [Resumed]
utterances.text: "... nor any concerted actions because the command was mindful of this in view of the fact that it was generally known that we as members of the Serbian Radical Party had clashed with the -- with Arkan's men already in Bijeljina. I knew Mile Gatarevic, called Bolero, from Brcko, and I know that he was not a member of the Serbian Radical Party and that he was not in my unit" --

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Very well. What is your impression? Is this a truthful statement on the part of Mirko Blagojevic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1058 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Perhaps. In all that, I would not agree that they returned from Brcko on the 17th of May because I saw him at a later date after that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Okay. I'll give you the proof that he returned on the 17th of May.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please quickly see document 3. This is the death certificate of Branislav Filipovic, Sumar, and the date of his burial in Bijeljina. Do you have it? The Judges have it. This is the death certificate for Branislav Filipovic, Sumar, proving that the burial was on the 16th of May. All members of Mirko Blagojevic's unit headed by him attended the funeral.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Do you see the death certificate?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1058 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: So Mirko Blagojevic had to be in the Luka camp before the 16th of May to take over the 20 imprisoned Muslims, to deliver them to the Muslim side, and to take over the dead body of his soldier. So it could not have been on the 29th of May. It could -- it had to be before the 16th of May. And now you see Mirko Blagojevic came to the Luka camp to take over 20 Muslim prisoners to be exchanged, and to the rest of you he brought cigarettes and cookies and he talked to you in a very civilised manner with a lot of respect. He addresses you as brethren. He takes 20 prisoners away. And you say that his men subsequently came back to beat you. You really don't think that I will believe you. Maybe the Trial Chamber will believe you, the OTP will believe you, but how can you think that I can believe you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1058 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Seselj, it seems that you were not listening. I never said that I was in Luka on the 17th of May. I was taken to Luka on the 26th of May, 1992, and I'm telling you what I saw in Luka. And that was on the 29th or the 30th of May. Mr. Mirko Blagojevic and his escorts were in Luka.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: You never stated that before. You have just made it up in order to grovel up to the OTP of The Hague Tribunal. And it is only in your statement that you did not provide yourself. It was done for you and sent to you by mail. And in none of the four previous cases did you say that Mirko Blagojevic was in Luka on the 29th or the 30th. I'm now giving you Mirko Blagojevic's statement testifying to his only arrival at Luka. Let's look at another thing. Let's look at the book by Jusuf Trbic. Did you ever hear of Jusuf Trbic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1058 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, never.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: He's a Muslim intellectual who published a book entitled "The Masters of the Darkness."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please finish your question.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is my last question, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Let's look at the document, this is document number 2, six pages, but we won't read them. The title page, Jusuf Trbic, "The Masters of the Darkness," and then on the second page you see the name of the publisher. And then we see that the publisher was the Kujundzic company based in Lukavac Tuzla. Do you agree?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1058 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Do you agree that that's where the book was published? And he gives a Muslim perspective of the war. But what makes it interesting is this: On page 5, the last paragraph speaks about the burial in the "sehid", burial ground, in Bijeljina, and he says: "Among all the political parties, only members of the Serbian Radical Party, Mr. Vojislav Seselj, was there ..." Can you see that? And he's a Muslim writer. Do you see on the sixth page, that's where he says or he announces the protest of the Serbian Chetnik Movement of North-Eastern Bosnia, signed by Mirko Blagojevic, against the crimes against Bijeljina, Muslims in the night between 24th and 25th of September, when 14 members of the Sarajlic family and 8 members of the Sejmenovic family were killed. Do you see how harsh Mirko Blagojevic is in his protest? Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1058 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And it is brought by a Muslim author in his book recognising Mirko Blagojevic's protest. And you are telling us here that Mirko Blagojevic's men beat prisoners in the Luka camp?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1058 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they did, Mr. Seselj.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: You made it up completely. You made it up subsequently to please the OTP in order to please the OTP because they don't have any proof against either me or the Serb radical. They want to find anything. And we don't see it in your previous statements; we only see it in one statement of yours. You wanted to be a protected witness only in these proceedings; before that, you testified in open court. I believe that you're more truthful there. Only because you were telling lies you wanted to testify under protection measures because you're ashamed of the lies that you've told us today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, would you like to respond that you are making a false statement, false testimony?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Mr. Seselj, I'm not here either to please the Prosecutor or anybody. I want to please the Judges and you yourself. Whatever I said before this Tribunal in the past is the truth. It is not my intention, Mr. Seselj, to accuse the Serbian people for what happened in Bosnia. It is my intention, if you will, to participate in assisting the Tribunal to learn the truth.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Why did you ask for protection measures today and never before?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1058 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because, Mr. Seselj, because members of your party in (redacted) still to this very day most of them are either criminals or people with limited memories, (redacted)

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1058 [Resumed]
utterances.text: (redacted) is a small place, Mr. Seselj, everything travels -- every news travels fast there. And you know very well that you're politically very powerful in (redacted).

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: How can you can be powerful politically in (redacted), because there's nobody but criminals in my party there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1058 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not only criminals, there are other people there. But most of them are criminals and radical elements.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: You're a clever person, a smart person. You're saying that I'm politically powerful in (redacted) and everybody in my party is criminal.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can you see this, Judges, how can I be powerful if only the worst criminals are in my party? How can I be politically powerful then? Criminals are somewhere else, and criminals are false witnesses. Bear that in mind.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Seselj, we are stopping now. Witness, you must stay where you are because you've been granted a protective measure. I would like to thank you for having come to testify at the request of the Trial Chamber. I know, Mr. Mussemeyer, that you wanted to take the floor for a few minutes. Can you take the floor in the presence of the witness, or do we need to drop the blinds and the witness needs to leave the courtroom?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUSSEMEYER
utterances.text: I just have two little issues. The first is your question how it comes that the notary has a date given of March of this year. If you look at what is written there, it says that it's the commission expiry. Above the last line, there is the date 11/12/08. So I think this is a misunderstanding. He signed -- the notary signed it on -- in November 2008, and his commission expires at March of this year. And, with your permission, I would like to ask the witness only one question in re-direct.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, there can be no re-direct. You send him your questions by mail.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There is no re-direct after the questions of the Judges. I'd like to turn to my colleagues and confirm this. So there is no re-direct. Mr. Marcussen, I thought you wanted to say something concerning a housekeeping matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think in light of the time, we don't need to go into these matters today. I can wait or address them in another way. But I would say this, though. It has been suggested today that the Prosecution has somehow fabricated a statement and sent it to the witness for him to sign. That is incorrect, and the Prosecution will look into this. As we cannot re-direct the witness on this, we may be presenting other evidence to show how this statement came into being. But the Prosecution has not just somehow sent the statement off by -- and instructed the witness to sign the statement. That is incorrect, and it was improper the way this was put by the accused.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUSSEMEYER
utterances.text: May I add half a sentence. I remember --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I did not say that the witness said that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Mussemeyer.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUSSEMEYER
utterances.text: I remember that the statement went back and forth several times because the witness made corrections to the -- to details of the statement. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. To finish off, we have already overstepped our time. We have four witnesses left, not five, four. We are currently checking their state of health, and as soon as one of them can come and testify, he will take the stand. But I would like to be extremely clear. If the medical reports are such that and the experts say that these witnesses cannot come and testify, then the -- then Rule 92 quater will apply. Everything rests on the assessment of the physicians for the moment. The court stands adjourned.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 7.04 p.m.
